points.description: States that the disadvantage is extra memory/space: each node of a doubly-linked list must store an additional pointer (the back/previous pointer) in addition to the next pointer.
points.partial_credit: Half (1.5): says it uses more memory/space but does not identify the extra pointer per node as the cause.

points.description: Identifies the extra space specifically as the back (previous) pointer stored in every node, i.e. two pointers per node versus one in a basic (singly) linked list.
points.partial_credit: Half (1): mentions extra pointers but does not say back/previous or does not contrast with the single pointer in a basic list.

rubric.notes: Full marks need both: extra space/memory as the disadvantage, and the cause stated precisely as the additional back (previous) pointer per node versus one pointer in a singly linked list. Vague answers such as "more complex" or "slower" earn nothing. A wrong claim, such as saying it is slower to traverse as the main disadvantage, loses the point it affects.
